title: Pick first model/OCR provider implementation
description: ARCHITECTURE.md isolates the provider behind analyzeLabel/verifyLabel. First concrete impl is undecided. Candidates: Anthropic vision (note F-042 supply-chain risk), OpenAI vision, local Tesseract+small LLM, hosted OCR + LLM split. Decide based on: TTB network restrictions (F-025), 5-second perceived-latency target, prototype budget. Document choice in ARCHITECTURE.md and add provider impl behind the interface.
notes: Decision: Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (released 2026-02-19), via the Gemini API directly. Rationale recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md > Model Provider Boundary. Anthropic excluded on procurement grounds (F-042). xAI excluded — grok-vision still beta. OpenAI GPT-5.5 viable fallback but ~17% behind on MMMU-Pro and 2.5x more expensive. Provider interface narrowed: analyzeLabel on provider, verifyLabel is domain logic (core/verification.ts) operating on ExtractedFields. Verification is two-layer per F-045/REQ-011: Layer 1 well-formedness (deterministic), Layer 2 comparison (hybrid: deterministic for warning/ABV/contents, LLM-assisted via the same Gemini provider for brand/class). Production swap path: Vertex AI Government / Azure OpenAI / Bedrock per TTB procurement catalog.

title: Pick SQL access library: Knex vs Kysely
description: ARCHITECTURE.md currently picks Knex; Chair is leaning toward Kysely. Tower writes a short comparison covering: type-safety with TS-strict (Kysely's strength), migration ergonomics (Knex's strength, mature CLI), reviewer familiarity (Knex more conventional, Kysely growing), ecosystem maturity, exit cost if we change later. Output: a 1-paragraph decision recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md and a rewrite of the existing Knex mentions in 'Chosen Stack', 'Why This Stack', and 'Database Responsibilities' sections. Blocks cc-scz so scaffolding doesn't bake in the wrong choice.
notes: Decision: Kysely. Rationale: schema-first type inference aligns with the project's strict TS rules (no any, no casts, noUncheckedIndexedAccess); the shared Database interface doubles as documentation between API and worker; column typos become compile errors. Migration tooling gap (no Knex-style CLI) is small at our scale — a tsx-driven Migrator script is sufficient for ~4-6 expected migrations. Reviewer surprise minimal in 2026. ARCHITECTURE.md updated; cc-scz design notes updated to install kysely + pg + tsx.

title: Vertical slice: ingestion + worker + stub verifier + review UI
description: First end-to-end pass: Express server, Chokidar watcher (subscribed to .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp AND .json with awaitWriteFinish enabled), worker entry point, Kysely migrations for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results tables, a stubbed analyzeLabel provider returning fixed ExtractedFields, a stubbed verifyLabel (in core/verification.ts) returning plausible Layer 1 + Layer 2 per-field results without calling a real model, queue-first React+Vite review UI listing processed/queued/awaiting_label/failed/needs_review. The watcher pairs files by filename stem per F-046/REQ-012: upsert job by stem; image-first creates job and runs Layer 1 with Layer 2 reporting needs_application_data; json-first creates job in awaiting_label state with no Layer runs; later arrival of the sibling file triggers Layer 1 (if newly available) or Layer 2 re-run (if image was already processed). Goal: a label dropped in data/incoming/ ends up reviewable in the UI within seconds. Deps: cc-scz scaffolding task.
design: Consumes: cc-scz scaffolding (package.json, tsconfig, Kysely + pg, docker-compose, data/ dirs). Produces: working ingestion -> Layer 1/2 stub -> review UI. Key files (planning, may shift): src/server/index.ts, src/server/routes/jobs.ts (list, get), src/server/routes/upload.ts (multipart label+json), src/worker/index.ts, src/worker/watcher.ts (chokidar subscribed to image+json globs, awaitWriteFinish on, upsert-by-stem), src/worker/pair.ts (stem matching, sibling lookup), src/core/providers/types.ts (LabelProvider interface with analyzeLabel), src/core/providers/stub.ts (stub returning fixed ExtractedFields), src/core/verification.ts (verifyLabel({extracted, application}) returning {layer1, layer2}), src/core/schemas.ts (Zod for ApplicationData + provider boundary), src/db/schema.ts (Kysely Database interface for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results), src/db/migrations/001_init.ts, src/web/* (Vite React SPA: queue list view, single job detail showing Layer 1 and Layer 2 results separately). Job status enum: queued, awaiting_label, processing, processed, needs_review, failed. ApplicationData schema per F-046: brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin?. Government warning is NOT in ApplicationData (regulation-defined). Stubs: analyzeLabel returns plausible ExtractedFields; verifyLabel returns mixed pass/fail/needs_review across Layer 1 and Layer 2 to exercise the UI.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Drop a paired image+JSON into data/incoming/ -> a job appears in the UI within seconds with Layer 1 and Layer 2 results populated. 2. Drop only an image -> job appears with Layer 1 results and Layer 2 marked needs_application_data. 3. Drop only a JSON -> job appears in awaiting_label state with no Layer results. 4. Drop the missing sibling later -> existing job is updated (no duplicate created); Layer 2 re-runs without re-running Layer 1 in the image-first case; both layers run in the JSON-first case. 5. Browser upload of a paired or label-only submission produces the same internal representation. 6. UI distinguishes Layer 1 (well-formedness) vs Layer 2 (comparison) results visually. 7. npm run typecheck, lint, test all pass on the resulting code. 8. No real Gemini call yet — that comes in a follow-up task.
